analysis.title: Credit Strategy Weekly: More treats than tricks
key_insights: Credit markets recovered this week after sharp widening in prior weeks, helped by more stable sovereign bonds and oil. SG expects some of the lost ground to be regained but no longer expects spreads to hit previous year-end forecasts.
SG sees a little respite into year-end, then renewed pressure, with wider spreads expected in 1H27.

Issues behind the widening are unresolved: oil is volatile and rising, the Middle East war is uncertain and sovereign bonds are volatile. Eurozone growth surprised to the upside (French numbers disappointed) and earnings remain healthy.
SG says stability in sovereign bonds is the key. If yields move in gentle ranges, even if higher, credit can gain further ground.

Euro primary issuance was EUR19bn this week excluding Friday deals, vs EUR17.3bn last week. October total EUR51.7bn, year-to-date EUR765.7bn. SG expects November to be very strong but now sees volumes surpassing the EUR871.4bn 2025 record only by year-end.
SG economists expect the Fed to hike once more by March 2027 (and in December per the market review), and the ECB to hike one or two more times. FOMC and ECB held rates this week.

Next week brings the US midterm elections on Tuesday, with Democrats expected to do well, plus NFP on Friday and the second busiest week of 3Q earnings. SG says another sharp deterioration in the Middle East or higher sovereign volatility would very likely push spreads wider.

Euro IG index (iBoxx Corporates) closed at B+116bp, 6bp tighter on the week, after hitting a year-wide of 122.5bp on Monday. It remains 26bp wider than at end-2025. HY closed at B+395.5bp, about 22bp tighter on the week and 43bp wider on the month.
Positioning: overweight USD IG vs EUR IG, overweight EUR IG vs HY, overweight financials, utilities, real estate and corporate hybrids, underweight retail and senior non-financials.
3Q earnings: 55% of European companies beat vs 36% missed. In the US, 80% beat vs 14% missed. Earnings growth is about 32% in Europe and 27% in the US.
Brent futures closed the week at the highest level in over a decade, around $117, with some contracts near $120. Credit yields: euro IG 4.39%, euro HY about 7.09%, USD IG 6.19%, USD HY 8.28%.

earnings_insights: 3Q season, Europe: 55% of companies beat expectations vs 36% missed, slightly ahead of prior seasons. US: 80% beat vs 14% missed, just below the two previous seasons. Over 70% of European and 86% of US companies will have reported by the end of next week.
Earnings growth is about 32% on average for European companies and about 27% for US companies, with almost all sectors growing again.

tension_points.bull_case: Fundamentals are solid, earnings are strong and growth is holding, so credit can recover gently into year-end if sovereign yields move in gentle ranges.
tension_points.bear_case: Oil is high and rising, the Middle East war is unresolved and sovereign bonds are volatile, so SG expects wider spreads in 1H27.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Another sharp deterioration in the Middle East, or an increase in sovereign bond volatility, would very likely push credit spreads wider across the board.

theme_stances.key_argument: Credit can recover gently into year-end on stable sovereign bonds, but not fully, with wider spreads expected in 1H27.
theme_stances.evidence: we no longer expect them to recover fully
